title: CPT covariance of the kinematic structures and of every action
text:
\emph{CPT covariance.} CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional invariant (T14, Proposition 5.2, its first premise: ``checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add'').

\emph{The conjugation.} CPT conjugation $\phi$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate exchanging the two families of maximal isotropic subspaces (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). Because of the reversal, $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism of the Clifford algebra.

\emph{Convention (field action).} $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$, so that curvature is carried by that automorphism. In this convention $\phi$ acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$ of the identity component, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, a real-linear one reversing that action (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So CPT conjugation is antilinear on the complexified ambient and on the Fock module, of Wigner's antiunitary type (argued there, not proved).

\emph{Action clause.} For every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, the gauge couplings among its parameters $\mu$ included, $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$; in particular $C$ does not move $\mu$.

\emph{What is checked and what is premised.} Checked: the fibre metric, the completion, the pairing on the Fock module, and the frozen point's action, which with every functional of real tensor fields invariant under constant $SO_{0}(2,4)$ satisfies the action clause in this convention by the cited result's clause (5). Premised: the imported gauge sector, spinor and fermion fields, and structures later papers add. For the gauge sector the standard CPT theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory; that this conjugation realises that operator is argued, not proved, so the gauge sector's invariance ``is imported and carried as a premise''.

title: H: the second stage is hierarchical

title: Introduction
Introduction
text:
The neutrino was the largest gap in the framework's derived content. This paper addresses it using only parts already present in the series, and ends by registering the framework's most precise and most exposed prediction: this is, by design and by declaration, the series' fastest-falsifiable paper, published while the prediction is still open.

The chain. The Standard-Model paper T12's derived content always contained a fourth colour singlet: the single-twistor sector carries \emph{two} singlets, at grades zero and three of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3}$, and the observed comparison column always had two. The right-handed neutrino is the grade-zero state, the \emph{empty twistor}, the pair system with no rung occupied, whose hypercharge the weight rule computes as zero. Anomaly cancellation could not have fixed it: with a fourth singlet of free hypercharge and $Y_{Q} \neq 0$ the anomaly-free spectra are exactly the two-dimensional span of the derived spectrum and $B - L$, a fact we prove in closed form, so the zero is a computation of the content derivation and not a consistency condition, and the Standard Model's ambivalence about $\nu_{R}$ is the ambivalence of a bottom-up construction that has only anomalies to go on. The natural small-mass mechanism is refuted first (the sixteenth refutation): the cosmological term of the mass paper T11's deformed bracket lies below the flat term by $\Lambda l^{2}/6$ for a composite of extent $l$, and can dominate only at horizon size. Gauge invariance then singles out the Majorana bilinear of the total singlet as the one fermion mass term that carries no charge and needs no condensate, an elementary fact proved outright and using nothing from the framework; whether the framework's own mass bracket, which T12 computes only on slot states and about which it says nothing for slot-free states, realises that term, and at what scale $M$, is a premise this paper names rather than derives, and with it the light masses follow by block inversion. Indifference makes the Majorana matrix $S_{3}$-invariant, which we show means $\alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J$ with $\J$ the all-ones matrix and, in the Gram-square reading, $\alpha = 0$ at leading order: the democratic vector is an eigenvector, and the seesaw of the democratic Dirac matrix is rank one at leading order and scalar on the democratic block, $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$, whatever $\alpha$ is. Three numbers follow: the ordering is normal (inverted excluded by rank plus small corrections, not by fit); the sum is bounded below by the oscillation floor and is at it, $\mnu \approx 0.059$ eV, if the second stage of the breaking is hierarchical; and the effective double-beta mass is one of two values, $1.5$ or $3.7$ meV, if the breaking is real. These are consequences of $m_{1} \approx 0$ and real phases, shared with any model having those two features; what the framework adds is the structure that produces them. The sum is at the exact centre of the sharpest tension in current cosmology, and the framework cannot use the community's standard way of relaxing the bound (a varying dark-energy equation of state) because it predicts $w = -1$: the two stances are one joint prediction. Finally, the heavy states that make the masses are the textbook mechanism of leptogenesis, and that mechanism is suppressed in three steps (alignment, a reheating premise at the lower heavy scale, phases), at the cost of a fifth registered stance: $\delta_{CP} \in \{0, \pi\}$.

title: Point of contact: why the neutrino is different
text: Every other fermion of the derived content has at least one pair mode occupied and is charged under something; the neutrino's right-handed partner is the one state with no mode occupied and nothing to be charged under: the empty pair system, the total singlet. The physics the seesaw needs (a fermion whose mass term requires no condensate) is exactly what a total singlet has in any gauge theory (a neutral bilinear with itself), and the section ``The seesaw, and its premises'' turns that match into the mechanism as far as gauge invariance can carry it, which is not as far as the framework's own bracket goes: that bracket is computed only on slot-occupying states, and T12 declares it undefined for an excited composite and says nothing about slot-free states (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-mass-bracket-quantum-numbers}), so the framework has not yet said which of its objects, if any, is the neutral bilinear of two grade-zero states. The reading explains the Standard Model's ambivalence, and Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}(2) makes the explanation exact: a bottom-up construction has only anomaly cancellation to fix hypercharges, and anomaly cancellation is insensitive to a fourth singlet, so it can neither require nor forbid $\nu_{R}$ nor fix its charge; a top-down content derivation computes the state and its weight, and carries it necessarily.

title: The seesaw, and its premises
The seesaw: what gauge invariance proves, and what is assumed
proof: (1) With $\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} = 0$ and $C = 0$, $m = \sqrt{2}|B_{\Lambda}| = \sqrt{2}\,\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}|[\omega\omega]|$ by Fact \claimref{mass.exact-join}. The ratio of the two terms of $B_{\Lambda}$ is $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,l^{2}p/p = \Lambda l^{2}/6$, equal to one at $l^{2} = 6/\Lambda = 2\LH^{2}$. For the $\Lambda$-term neutrino, $|[\omega\omega]| = 6m/(\sqrt{2}\Lambda)$; with $p = m$ this gives $l^{2} = 6/(\sqrt{2}\Lambda) = \sqrt{2}\,\LH^{2}$, so $l/\LH = 2^{1/4}$ exactly, independent of $\Lambda$ and of $m$; with $p = 100$ GeV and $\Lambda \in (1.0, 1.2) \times 10^{-52}$ m$^{-2}$ \cite{PDG2024} the script brackets $l$ inside $(1.3, 1.5) \times 10^{20}$ m by exact interval arithmetic on the eV-metre conversion. The Casimir branch: $C = 3m^{2}/\Lambda$ at $m = 0.05$ eV lies in $(1.6, 2.0) \times 10^{63}$ (script). (2) The hypercharges of the derived content are Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-derived-content-singlets}'s; a bilinear of fields of hypercharges $Y_{1}, Y_{2}$ transforms with $Y_{1} + Y_{2}$ under the abelian factor, so it is neutral if and only if $Y_{1} + Y_{2} = 0$. Over the six fields, the only pair summing to zero is $(N, N)$ (the script checks all twenty-one pairs); $L N$ carries $-\tfrac12$, absorbed by the condensate of charge $\tfrac12$. (3) Under (M) (\claimref{neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale}), let $\begin{psmallmatrix} x \\ y \end{psmallmatrix}$ be an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\mu$: $\mD y = \mu x$ and $\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x + M_{R}y = \mu y$. For $\mu$ of order $\|\mD\|^{2}/\|M_{R}\|$ the second equation gives $y = -(M_{R} - \mu)^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x = -M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x + O(\mu\|M_{R}\|^{-2})$, and substituting, $\mu x = -\mD M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x$ to leading order; the light block is $\mD\,(-M_{R}^{-1})\,\mD^{\mathsf{T}}$, a congruence of a symmetric matrix, hence symmetric. The script assembles the block matrix and checks the exact elimination identity $\begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & \mD \\ \mD^{\mathsf{T}} & M_{R}\end{psmallmatrix}\begin{psmallmatrix} x \\ -M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x\end{psmallmatrix} = \begin{psmallmatrix} -\mD M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}}x \\ 0\end{psmallmatrix}$ on rational instances; in the scalar case the eigenvalues of $\begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & m_{D} \\ m_{D} & M_{R}\end{psmallmatrix}$ are $\tfrac12(M_{R} \pm \sqrt{M_{R}^{2} + 4m_{D}^{2}})$, and the script certifies by exact square-root brackets that the small one lies within $m_{D}^{4}/M_{R}^{3}$ of $-m_{D}^{2}/M_{R}$.

title: $S_{3}$-invariant symmetric matrices
text: Let $\J$ be the $3 \times 3$ all-ones matrix and $u' = (1,1,1)$. A real symmetric $3 \times 3$ matrix $S$ satisfies $PSP^{\mathsf{T}} = S$ for every permutation matrix $P$ if and only if $S = \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J$ for real $\alpha, \beta$. Such an $S$ has $u'$ as an eigenvector with eigenvalue $M_{3} := \alpha + 3\beta$, the plane $u'^{\perp}$ as an eigenspace with eigenvalue $\alpha$, $\det S = \alpha^{2}(\alpha + 3\beta)$, hence is invertible if and only if $\alpha \neq 0$ and $\alpha \neq -3\beta$, with $S^{-1} = \alpha^{-1}\mathbf{1} - \beta\,\alpha^{-1}(\alpha + 3\beta)^{-1}\J$. Writing $\Pi = \mathbf{1} - \J/3$ for the projector on $u'^{\perp}$, $S = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$, and $S^{-1} = \alpha^{-1}\Pi + M_{3}^{-1}\J/3$ when both are nonzero.
proof: Invariance under the transposition $(12)$ gives $S_{11} = S_{22}$ and $S_{13} = S_{23}$; under $(23)$, $S_{22} = S_{33}$ and $S_{12} = S_{13}$; so all diagonal entries equal some $\alpha + \beta$ and all off-diagonal entries equal some $\beta$, that is $S = \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J$; conversely $\mathbf{1}$ and $\J$ are fixed by every $P$. Since $\J u' = 3u'$ and $\J v = 0$ for $v \perp u'$, the spectrum is as stated and $\det S = \alpha^{2}(\alpha + 3\beta)$. The inverse follows from $\J^{2} = 3\J$: $(\alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J)(\alpha^{-1}\mathbf{1} + \gamma\J) = \mathbf{1} + (\alpha\gamma + \beta\alpha^{-1} + 3\beta\gamma)\J$, which is $\mathbf{1}$ for $\gamma = -\beta/(\alpha(\alpha + 3\beta))$. The projector form is $\Pi\J = 0$, $\Pi^{2} = \Pi$, $(\J/3)^{2} = \J/3$. The script verifies the characterisation on positive and negative instances over all six permutations, the spectrum, the determinant with both singular loci, the inverse against the adjugate, and the projector form on rational instances.

title: The rank-one seesaw: ordering, sum, and the double-beta values
proof: (0) With $\mD = d\J$ (the democratic alignment of Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-indifference-faces-democratic-alignment-rank}) and $\J v = 0$ for $v \in u'^{\perp}$, $\mD$ annihilates $u'^{\perp}$ on the right and has image along $u'$; in the basis $(u', u'^{\perp})$ of both the light and the heavy sector, the $6 \times 6$ mass matrix is block diagonal with the $2 \times 2$ democratic block (entries $\mD u' = 3d\,u' = m_{D}u'$ and $M_{R}u' = M_{3}u'$) and the $u'^{\perp}$ blocks ($0$ for the light states, $\alpha\mathbf{1}_{2}$ for $N_{\perp}$, no Dirac entry). The democratic block is the one-generation seesaw of Proposition \claimref{neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what}(3), under (M) (\claimref{neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale}), giving $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$ at leading order. When $\alpha \neq 0$ and $M_{3} \neq 0$ the same follows from the full inversion of Lemma \claimref{neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices}: $\J M_{R}^{-1}\J = \J(\alpha^{-1}\Pi + M_{3}^{-1}\J/3)\J = 3M_{3}^{-1}\J$ since $\J\Pi = 0$, so the light matrix is $(3d^{2}/M_{3})\J$ with eigenvalue $9d^{2}/M_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{3}$. The script verifies the block decomposition, the identity $\J M_{R}^{-1}\J = 3M_{3}^{-1}\J$, and the light matrix on several rational $(\alpha, \beta, d)$, and separately that the seesaw of a rank-one $\mD$ is rank one for every invertible $M_{R}$, $S_{3}$-invariant or not. (1) Inverted ordering has $m_{1}^{2} = m_{2}^{2} - \Delta m^{2}_{21}$ with $m_{2}^{2} \ge \Delta m^{2}_{31}$, so $m_{1}/m_{2} \ge \sqrt{1 - \Delta m^{2}_{21}/\Delta m^{2}_{31}} > 0.98$ at the measured splittings (script). (2) The floor and the values at $m_{1} = 0.1, 1, 3, 10$ meV are computed by exact rational interval arithmetic on the splitting brackets; so is $m_{2}/m_{3} \in (0.16, 0.18)$ and the inverted floor $(0.097, 0.102)$ eV used in Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.confrontation-it-stands-date-stamped}. (3) Under (H, \claimref{neutrino.h-second-stage-hierarchical}), $m_{\beta\beta} = |c_{13}^{2}s_{12}^{2}m_{2}e^{i\phi} + s_{13}^{2}m_{3}e^{i\phi'}| + O(m_{1})$; at $\phi - \phi' \in \{0, \pi\}$ the script brackets the two values from the angle and splitting brackets, and separately certifies that at $m_{1} = 0.1$ meV both move by less than $0.1$ meV and that at $m_{1} = 1$ meV the four real sign patterns already span $0.6$-$4.6$ meV, which is what fixes the strength at which (H) is stated.

title: The breaking relation
text:
Let $\mD = d(\J + \delta A)$ with $A$ a real $3 \times 3$ matrix (its scale is fixed by the reference direction $e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$, the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction, for which $\|\Pi A\Pi\| = \tfrac23$ in the operator norm and $\lambda_{A} = \tfrac49$ below; $\delta$ is quoted relative to that direction, as the instances state, and $\delta^{2}\lambda_{A}$ is invariant under a rescaling of $A$), $\delta$ a real breaking parameter, and $M_{R} = \alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3$ with $\alpha, M_{3} \neq 0$. Then, exactly,
\[
\mD M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}} \;=\; \frac{d^{2}\delta^{2}}{\alpha}\,A\,\Pi\,A^{\mathsf{T}} \;+\; \frac{d^{2}}{3M_{3}}\,q\,q^{\mathsf{T}}, \qquad q = (\J + \delta A)\,u' = 3u' + \delta A u' .
\]
Consequently the second and third light masses are, to leading order in $\delta$, $(d^{2}\delta^{2}/\alpha)$ times the two eigenvalues $\lambda_{A} \ge \lambda'_{A}$ of the compression $\Pi A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}\Pi$ of the first term to $u'^{\perp}$ (not of $A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}$ itself, whose range is not orthogonal to $u'$), so $m_{1}/m_{2} = \lambda'_{A}/\lambda_{A}$ at this order, and
\[
\frac{m_{2}}{m_{3}} \;=\; \frac{\delta^{2}\lambda_{A}}{9}\,\frac{M_{3}}{\alpha}\,\Bigl(1 + O(\delta) + O\bigl(\delta^{2}M_{3}/\alpha\bigr)\Bigr):
\]
no breaking of the Majorana sector alone lifts $m_{2}$ (since $\J X \J = (\textstyle\sum_{ij}X_{ij})\J$ for every $X$), the Dirac breaking enters squared, and the seesaw enhances it by $M_{3}/\alpha$. The second remainder is $O(m_{2}/m_{3})$, a function of the answer itself, and does not vanish as $\delta \to 0$ at fixed physical ratio; at the sizes of interest the two together are not small (the formula overestimates the exact ratio by more than a half at the instance of Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}), so the instances are diagonalised exactly rather than read from the formula.
proof: $M_{R}^{-1} = \alpha^{-1}\Pi + M_{3}^{-1}\J/3$ by Lemma \claimref{neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices}. Expand $\mD M_{R}^{-1}\mD^{\mathsf{T}} = d^{2}(\J + \delta A)(\alpha^{-1}\Pi + M_{3}^{-1}\J/3)(\J + \delta A^{\mathsf{T}})$. Since $\J\Pi = \Pi\J = 0$, the $\Pi$ term leaves only $\alpha^{-1}\delta^{2}A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}$; since $\J = u'u'^{\mathsf{T}}$, the $\J/3$ term is $M_{3}^{-1}\tfrac13\,(\J + \delta A)u'u'^{\mathsf{T}}(\J + \delta A^{\mathsf{T}}) = M_{3}^{-1}\tfrac13\,qq^{\mathsf{T}}$. The identity $\J X\J = (\sum X_{ij})\J$ is $u'^{\mathsf{T}}Xu' = \sum_{ij}X_{ij}$. The second term is rank one along $q = 3u' + O(\delta)$ with eigenvalue $d^{2}|q|^{2}/(3M_{3}) = 9d^{2}/M_{3}\,(1 + O(\delta))$; at fixed $\alpha$ and $M_{3}$ the first term is $O(\delta^{2})$ and the second $O(1)$, so to leading order in $\delta$ the second dominates, the top eigenvector of the sum is $q + O(\delta^{2}M_{3}/\alpha)$, and the remaining two eigenvalues are those of the first term compressed to $q^{\perp} = u'^{\perp} + O(\delta)$: that is, $(d^{2}\delta^{2}/\alpha)$ times the eigenvalues of $\Pi A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}\Pi$. (The range of $A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}$ is $A(u'^{\perp})$, which is not orthogonal to $u'$ unless $A^{\mathsf{T}}u' \parallel u'$, so the eigenvalues of the first term itself are not the light masses; for $A = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ the two differ by the factor $\tfrac23$ exactly.) The script verifies the exact identity on rational instances of $(\alpha, \beta, d, \delta, A)$; for $A = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ (the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction, $\lambda_{A} = \tfrac49$, $\lambda'_{A} = 0$) it diagonalises the light matrix exactly, the characteristic polynomial factoring as $\lambda$ times a quadratic, and certifies $m_{2}/m_{3} \in (0.168, 0.172)$ at $\delta = 0.286$ and $M_{3}/\alpha = 66$ (the instance of Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}), against $0.267$ from the leading-order formula there; and, at the small-breaking end, that the exact ratio at $\delta = 0.006$ is within four percent of the $\lambda_{A} = \tfrac49$ formula and about two thirds of the $A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}$ one.

title: The branch: $\alpha \ll M_{3}$
text: The measured $m_{2}/m_{3} \approx 0.17$ and Lemma \claimref{neutrino.breaking-relation} leave two branches. With $\alpha$ of order $M_{3}$ the Dirac breaking would need $\delta$ of order one, which is not a perturbation and would void the second-order language and the analogy behind Premise (H). With $\alpha \ll M_{3}$ the breaking stays a correction. The size of $\delta$ is calibrated against the paper's own texture: a charged-lepton matrix $c(\J + \delta_{c}e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}})$ reproduces $m_{\mu}/m_{\tau} \approx 0.0595$ \cite{PDG2024} at $\delta_{c} = 0.286$ by exact singular values (the leading-order relation is $m_{\mu}/m_{\tau} = \tfrac29\delta_{c}$), and if the Dirac neutrino breaking is of the same size in the same direction, an assumption made for the instance, then the measured $m_{2}/m_{3}$ is met at $M_{3}/\alpha \approx 66$ by exact diagonalisation (the perturbative root; the exact ratio is not monotone in $M_{3}/\alpha$, peaking near $0.24$ at about $176$, and a second root past the peak lies where the lemma's remainders dominate), that is $\alpha/M_{3} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-2}$; $\delta$ and $M_{3}/\alpha$ are the two parameters of a fitted instance, not a test, and $M_{3}/\alpha$ scales as $\delta^{-2}$. This paper takes the second branch, and it is the one the Gram-square reading supplies: $M_{R} \propto \J$ at leading order means $\alpha = 0$ there, and $\alpha$ arises at the order of the breaking of the Majorana sector, $\alpha = \delta' M_{3}$, so that the measured ratio is a relation between the two breakings: at leading order $\delta^{2}\lambda_{A}/(9\delta')$, which the exact diagonalisation reduces to the measured $0.17$ at $\delta' = 1/66 \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-2}$ for $\delta = 0.286$ (the leading-order form would put $\delta'$ at $0.024$, an overestimate by more than a half at these sizes); a relation the second-order programme must satisfy and that this paper records rather than derives. Two consequences follow from the branch: the pair $N_{\perp}$ is near $\alpha \approx 9 \times 10^{12}$ GeV at the top of Hypothesis (U) (and near $5.1 \times 10^{9}$ GeV at its bottom), nearly two orders ($\log_{10}66 = 1.8$) below $M_{3}$; and the comparison of $0.17$ with the charged-sector ratios is not like for like, since the neutrino ratio carries the seesaw factor $M_{3}/\alpha$ that the charged ratios do not. The same lemma says what Premise (H) asks of the direction: the first term carries both $m_{2}$ and $m_{1}$, with $m_{1}/m_{2} = \lambda'_{A}/\lambda_{A}$ the eigenvalue ratio of $\Pi A\Pi A^{\mathsf{T}}\Pi$, so (H) is the statement that the first stage of the breaking is effectively rank one on $u'^{\perp}$, as the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction $e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ is exactly ($\lambda'_{A} = 0$), and as a generic direction is not. What fixes $\alpha$ and the direction is successor problem (2). On the Standard-Model paper's Pati-Salam route the Majorana matrix is $v_{R}f$, with $f$ the $126$ coupling the charged fermions share \cite[Fact~11.1, Prop.~11.5]{ButlerT12}, so there the texture is not free; that paper's fits reach the measured masses with textures of their own, the untuned one with $m_{1}$ inside Premise (H) \cite[Obs.~11.7]{ButlerT12}, and whether the branch taken here is among them is not settled.

title: Mixing: none at leading order
text: The structure delivers no large mixing by itself. The charged-lepton matrix and the light neutrino matrix are both rank one along the same democratic direction $u'$ at leading order, so their heavy eigenvectors coincide, the heavy-heavy mixing vanishes, and the mixing in the degenerate light plane is undetermined. All three observed angles must therefore come from the breaking, and the requirement is stated as a number: the observed $|U_{\tau 3}|^{2} = c_{13}^{2}c_{23}^{2}$ lies in $(0.39, 0.55)$ at $\sin^{2}\theta_{23} \in (0.44, 0.60)$ \cite{NuFIT2024}, so the two heavy eigenvectors, the charged lepton's and the neutrino's, must be separated by between about $42$ and $51$ degrees, about $47$ at the centre of the bracket (the conversion to degrees is not scripted). What the breaking of Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3} supplies at the $S_{3} \to S_{2}$ direction is a tilt of about $13$ degrees on the neutrino side and about $3$ on the charged side (unscripted estimates at that remark's instance); whether a breaking of the size that remark fixes can supply a near-maximal $\theta_{23}$ is open, and is the number successor problem (1) must meet. The PMNS numbers depend on the same breaking and are this paper's observation, not an import. The classic democratic-texture route to large angles (the quark-sector construction of \cite{HHW1978}, carried to the lepton sector by a later literature not cited here) needs a democratic charged-lepton matrix against a non-democratic neutrino one, which this structure does not supply at leading order. The script confirms that both leading forms have $u'$ as the eigenvector of their nonzero eigenvalue.

title: The valuation of $M$, at both ends of Hypothesis (U)
text: Premise (M) is valued, not derived. With $m_{3} \in (49.4, 50.5)$ meV, the scalar seesaw of Proposition \claimref{neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double}(0) gives $M_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/m_{3}$, and the Dirac eigenvalue is fixed only by the dark-matter paper's Hypothesis (U) (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-ceiling-under-hypothesis-u-arrow}): $M_{3} \approx 6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV if the neutrino's Dirac mass is retained unbroken like the top's ($m_{t} \in (172.28, 172.86)$ GeV, the PDG 2024 $172.57 \pm 0.29$ \cite{PDG2024}), $3.5 \times 10^{11}$ GeV if it is split like the bottom's ($m_{b} \in (4.13, 4.23)$ GeV \cite{PDG2024}), the two differing by $(m_{t}/m_{b})^{2} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{3}$, with a further order of magnitude of running systematic named there. The dark-matter paper's rung scale is the same quotient under the same hypothesis from the same datum, so the two papers agree by construction and not by test; deriving $M$ from the framework's own dynamics, which would turn the agreement into a check, is successor problem (3). $M_{3}$ lies below a unification scale taken at $M_{U} = 2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV by a factor of $33$ to $34$ at the top of the range and about $5.7 \times 10^{4}$ at the bottom (script-bracketed at that $M_{U}$; the factor scales with it). That $M_{U}$ is the Standard-Model paper's \emph{conditional} branch, the meeting of the couplings with partner-type intermediate content that it does not derive. Its other branch, an intermediate Pati-Salam symmetry from the split between slots and pairs, meets at $M_{U} \approx 3.4 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, above $M_{3}$ at either end, with an intermediate scale $M_{I} \approx 1.9 \times 10^{10}$ GeV \cite[Prop.~10.10]{ButlerT12}. On the derived content alone the couplings do not meet: the unification condition with the Standard-Model coefficients puts $M_{U}$ near $7 \times 10^{14}$ GeV, at which the factor at the top of the range is $1.16$ to $1.19$ to two places (script-bracketed at $(1.159, 1.192)$), while the pairwise meetings themselves fall at about $10^{13}$, $2 \times 10^{14}$ and $10^{17}$ GeV \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT12}; the lowest of these is at this paper's own $\alpha \approx 9 \times 10^{12}$ GeV at the top of Hypothesis (U) (Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}; at the bottom, $\alpha \approx 5.1 \times 10^{9}$ GeV, it lies three orders above), the ceiling Premise (R) imposes on the descent, so the consistency consequence of Proposition \claimref{neutrino.leptogenesis-suppressed-alignment-reheating-premise-new}(3) is confined to the two branches on which the couplings meet and is claimed only there. On the Pati-Salam branch the measured weak angle fixes the triplet vev, $v_{R} \approx 4.2 \times 10^{10}$ GeV, and with it the Dirac mass along the heavy direction, $m_{D} = 1.44\sqrt{f_{J}}$ GeV for a Majorana coupling $f_{J}$ there \cite[Prop.~11.2]{ButlerT12}: the bottom-like end of the range above, since a top-like $m_{D}$ would need $f_{J}$ near $4000$. This paper keeps both ends, its valuation resting on Hypothesis (U) and not on that branch; the series' Pati-Salam route selects the bottom one. On that branch $M_{I}$ lies between the two values of $\alpha$, above the bottom one and below the top one, so whether Premise (R) keeps the descent below the intermediate scale depends on the end.

title: The predictions
The double prediction: the sum predicted at the floor
text: Under Premise (H), the prediction of Proposition \claimref{neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double}(2) is at the exact centre of the sharpest tension in current cosmology, and the framework has no parameter to adjust (a figure of the original). The second data release of the baryon-acoustic survey with the microwave background gives $\mnu < 0.064$ eV at ninety-five percent confidence in $\Lambda$CDM \cite{DESI2025}. A four-author analysis combining the public microwave small-scale and baryon-acoustic likelihoods reports, in $\Lambda$CDM with adiabatic initial conditions, $\mnu < 0.052$ eV under a prior extending to zero, notes itself that the number lies \emph{below} the minimal normal-ordering value $0.0588$ eV and reads it as an artefact of the unphysical prior, and reports $\mnu < 0.092$ eV with the physical floor imposed; its isocurvature extension relaxes the adiabatic bound only to $0.057$ eV \cite{HouWangZhaoZhang2026}. The community's standard way of relaxing the bound is a varying dark-energy equation of state, which relaxes the bound substantially ($0.111$ eV in the same analysis under the two-parameter $w_{0}w_{a}$ form). This framework cannot use that option: Fact \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition} predicts $w = -1$ exactly, with no parameter to absorb a deviation, conditional only on the frozen point's definition off the vacuum region, which the dark-energy paper names, does not use, and shows cannot track the curvature; and that part of the prediction is itself under a contested three-to-four-sigma preference for evolution in the same data release, as Fact \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition} records. The two stances are therefore one joint prediction, registered as the framework's fourth and stated plainly: within the frozen-point cosmology the neutrino-mass tension must resolve \emph{at the floor}, the true sum is $0.059$ eV, the present bound below it is a prior artefact or systematics of the known lensing-anomaly and boundary sensitivities, and the ordering is normal. Registered at the level of its inputs, which are date-stamped and refreshed at submission.

title: The confrontation as it stands, date-stamped
text: This is the paper's most falsifiable claim: it may be settled within a data release or two, it cannot be adjusted after the fact, and it ties the dark-energy stance to the neutrino sector so that they survive or are refuted together. As of this writing the record is unusually favourable to the prediction's \emph{structure} while unusually tight on its \emph{number}. Three points, each refreshed at submission. The asymmetry: the arrow counted, and the fifteenth refutation
text:
The framework does not generate its asymmetry; it inherits it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Sakharov.)} The Sakharov conditions are for generating an asymmetry dynamically from a symmetric state; a universe whose asymmetry is initial data does not need them. The descent supplies the reason the initial data need not be symmetric: it is irreversible (the lossy projection of the taxonomy paper's descent theorem \cite{ButlerT1}), it creates the tower charges, and it makes one orientation choice, the Witt flag, which is what particle-versus-antiparticle means (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}). Each matches a Sakharov condition in name; none is a mechanism producing a number.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The fifteenth refutation.)} A pre-descent $\theta$-term would source asymmetry through the topology of gauge bundles; but it integrates a characteristic class, of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$, and at the P3 representatives a $\theta$-term exists exactly where a flag bit does. In this tower it is excluded empirically: a $\theta$-routed asymmetry needs an angle of order one at the descent that does not relax before it acts, and the neutron dipole bound $|d_{n}| < 1.8 \times 10^{-26}\,e\,$cm \cite{Abel2020} gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today (through a hadronic matrix element with its own uncertainty). Not excluded, and not claimed: an angle that relaxes or rolls; and the mirror's angle, which equals ours only by P2 along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)), the copy being of the functional, not its coefficient. Internally the paper says only that the orientation is the one mechanism the framework itself supplies; that locates the mechanism and does not refute the alternative.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Confinement and universality.)} The orientation route is one bit spent once (uniqueness among all conceivable mechanisms is not claimed). A flag exists on every rung of every tower (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}), but the flag \emph{bit} only in the even residues at their P3 representatives (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), so the asymmetry is confined to the oriented causal towers, this one and the mirror, and the odd towers carry none by either route. Universality of the value is Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers}, a theorem for the mirror (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)) and not extendable to inequivalent towers, the asymmetry per mode depending on the tower's own charge structure.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The value, a stance.)} $\epsilon$ is not derived here and not classified. The trichotomy's kinematic clause runs for it as for $N$ ($\epsilon$ is continuous), at that Fact's observation level; the dynamical clause does not, since generating an asymmetry from CPT-invariant dynamics is exactly what the Sakharov mechanism does. \emph{Stance, flagged and attacked in the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper'':} the framework inherits its asymmetry, and $\epsilon$ is initial data of the descent, refuted by any in-framework calculation that produces $\epsilon$ dynamically. The count uses only the equality of $\epsilon$ across the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), not its provenance. On the stance the unexplained numbers are two, $N$ and $\epsilon$, with the orientation bit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} a third datum of the same event.
\end{enumerate}

text:

With $m_{3}$ the heaviest light neutrino mass, the seesaw $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{R}$ then values the scale on which two results depend, in a range whose ends are the two readings of (U):
\[
\frac{m_{b}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 3.5 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV} \;\lesssim\; M_{\mathrm{rung}} \;=\; M_{R} \;=\; \frac{m_{D}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\lesssim\; \frac{m_{t}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV},

title: The orientation is the arrow: the seventeenth refutation
text:
The Standard-Model paper left one absolute bit undetermined, the particle-antiparticle orientation, expected to be fixed by the charge-zero condition. The expectation is refuted by a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ covariance argument parallel to the trichotomy's rescaling one, on three premises: that CPT conjugation $C$ is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} invariant, $S_{\mu}\circ C = S_{\mu}$, the gauge couplings included (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}; checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add); Hypothesis (S), under which the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, the source of the relative-versus-absolute split, is proved (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); and that the orientation flag is a datum of each solution, the sign of its complex structure relative to the Fock module's unit planted by the descent and not part of the kinematic structure (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}; were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space, hence dynamically fixed within each of two isomorphic theories, and the conclusion below would fail). Here $C$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate, an anti-automorphism; acting on fields as a symmetry does (vectors by its vector part, connections through the induced Lie algebra automorphism), it is $\mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation, so it is antilinear (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}).

Anything the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, and the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all \emph{relative} structure \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12}; under that reading the absolute bit is not kinematic, and since conjugation maps each solution space onto itself and exchanges the two orientations, the bit takes both values on every nonempty solution space: it is initial data in the sense of clause (I) of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, and so neither dynamically fixed nor a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are}). No exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives is used. It is the Witt flag of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}: the open orientation of the content derivation and the arrow of time are one choice, made once.

The descent measure carries two numbers and one bit. The neutrino sector supplies no orientation refutation condition: the identification of $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero is flag-covariant (the conjugate flag exchanges the singlet grades zero and three), so no completion of the orientation could exclude it \cite{ButlerT15}.

This is the seventeenth refutation (the sixteenth is the neutrino paper's \cite[Prop.~4.1(1)]{ButlerT15}), in the pattern of the thirteenth and the trichotomy: what the framework cannot determine, it can prove it cannot determine, and locate.

title: The alignment computed: the thirteenth refutation, democracy, and one heavy family
text:
Four statements, the first a refutation, the rest its redirection, each at the level marked.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The thirteenth refutation, by magnitude; a dimensional estimate.)} The source term of Proposition \claimref{families.source-term-linear-tilt-mass-functional} is $\Lambda$-suppressed, so the condensate it can induce is $\delta b \sim \Lambda\,\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ with $\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ a length; for any vacuum length between the Planck and Hubble scales, $\Lambda\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ lies between $H^{2}/M_{P} \approx 10^{-94}$ eV and $H \approx 10^{-33}$ eV, that is between roughly $10^{-105}$ and $10^{-44}$ of the weak scale $10^{11}$ eV: the tilt cannot reach $10^{2}$ GeV, the natural conjecture that the vacuum $\omega$-area sets the weak scale is refuted, and the weak scale falls back to the weight question, where the hierarchy has remained since the mass paper's fifth refutation.
\item \emph{(The redirection.)} Alignment requires only a nonzero tilt, and directions are ratios, $\Lambda$-independent; so what the vacuum $\omega$-area does determine is its \emph{direction} in the three-dimensional face space of Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite}, which carries the family ordering and the mixing. The magnitude was never the physical content; the direction is, and the direction is computable from symmetry where the magnitude was not.
\item \emph{(The direction, at structural level, under the Gram-square reading.)} The kinematic vacuum cannot break $S_{3}$ before its own source exists: a face-anisotropic vacuum would be uncaused structure, forbidden by the indifference instrument (Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument}). The source therefore lies on the democratic line, spanned by $u = (1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$. If the leading mass form is the Gram square of the source, $Y_{0} \propto u' u'^{\mathsf{T}}$ with $u' = (1,1,1)$, the democratic mass matrix of \cite{HHW1978} (the reading the section ``The Gaussian theorems'' realises at operator level and successor problem (2) asks to derive in general), then $Y_{0}$ has spectrum $(3, 0, 0)$ times the condensate scale: one heavy family and two light ones at leading order, the third generation's dominance as structure rather than fit; and Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite} is refined rather than replaced: the physical families are the \emph{eigenvectors} of the face-space mass form, at leading order the democratic vector (heavy) and its orthogonal plane (light), the faces up to the rotation the vacuum performs.
\item \emph{(The residue, named.)} The second-order breaking $S_{3} \to S_{2} \to 1$, the anisotropic corrections that lift the two light families and convert the CKM shape into CKM numbers: the family programme's next computable target, confronted in the section ``The Koide geometry''-the section ``The Gaussian theorems''. Everything in this proposition past the magnitude refutation is at the structural and observation levels stated.
\end{enumerate}

text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

title: Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). The $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ anomaly coefficient of the two doublets, $3Y_{Q} + Y_{L}$ with the three the colour multiplicity, is then the identity $3 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac12 = 0$; it would equal $1$ if the empty conformal spinor were listed as the particle instead, so the anomaly confirms the orientation the listing fixed. Pair counting fixes $|Y_{L}/Y_{Q}| = 3$; the parity fixes the sign.
\item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives
\[
(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},
\]
that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. (The listing by the opposite handedness is the conjugate of this one, the same spectrum in the opposite convention.) Under (S) the grade-$k$ states of a single conformal spinor are the $(0, k)$ components, the states with no slot mode and $k$ pair modes occupied (their content $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and weight $-2k$ match, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight), so their parity is the total parity and this listing is the same listing as in (1).
\item (Consistency, and uniqueness given the content; under (S) for the doublets.) With the content of (1) and (2), all four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} hold. Conversely, for the field content $Q = (2,3)$, $L = (2,1)$, $u^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $d^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $e^{c} = (1,1)$, all listed in one handedness, together with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or no fourth singlet, and $Y_{Q} = 1/6$ as the normalisation, the four conditions determine $Y_{L}$, $Y(e^{c})$ and $\{Y(u^{c}), Y(d^{c})\}$ uniquely, and the solution is the spectrum of (1) and (2). Both hypotheses are necessary: with a fourth singlet of unconstrained hypercharge the conditions admit a one-parameter family, and if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$ rather than zero.
\end{enumerate}

title: The internal symmetry ladder
text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form''.)

title: The mass bracket is a charged singlet
